page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.c6a.xlarge demonstrates modest performance characteristics. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance scores fall into the lower tier, registering at 767.9 and 1535.77 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only small block cached speeds at 200.72 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 16.16 GB/sec. However, the instance achieves average performance in specific tasks, such as single-threaded gzip compression at 23.96 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.24 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.xlarge offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not demand high memory capacity or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities, though the overall performance profile suggests it is best suited for light compute tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and entry-level application hosting rather than resource-intensive database operations or high-throughput data processing.
